text:
eng-sre-bot: ALERT: multiple eviction_spike events detected for cache=prefix-kv-store region=us-west-2. paging on-call.

Priya N.: seeing it in the API error matrix — routed 503s for streaming endpoints. hit-rate panel dropped from ~78% -> 14% over ~8m. looks correlated with a rollout of a new model shard?

Alex G.: I can confirm. cache_evictions/sec jumped ~7x at 11:12. backend logs show repeated OOMs in kv-proxy pod and fast LRU churn.

Maria S.: tagging incident-bot: customer-impact? which customers hit?

incident-bot: Customers with increased error rates: org-53 (playbooks), org-77 (analytics) — total 42 active requests affected in last 15m. Severity: S2 until mitigated.

Chris L.: mitigation idea: enable soft-evict mode and increase max-entries for prefix-kv-store by 20% in us-west-2 to reduce churn while we investigate hot prefixes. I'm going to push a config toggle to the canary cluster first.

Priya N.: +1 do a canary. Also let's add a quick prefix heatmap to see hot keys causing serial eviction. current Grafana panel only shows aggregate hit-rate.

Alex G.: rolling canary change now:
```bash
kubectl -n infra patch cm prefix-kv-config -p '{"data":{"evict_mode":"soft","max_entries":"120000"}}'
```
apply in canary-usw2. monitor ops-kv-proxy-*.

Maria S.: ack. I'll watch dashboards and customer errors. Oncall handover — @Priya N. will run the mitigation; I'll be available for escalations.

Priya N.: canary applied. ops-kv-proxy-0 memory steady, eviction/sec back down to baseline in canary. pushing to 50% of nodes next.

eng-sre-bot: deploy-bot reported rollout to canary-usw2 succeeded (3/3 pods).

Chris L.: good progress. early data: hit-rate for prefix-kv-store in canary nodes jumped from 14% -> 66% after soft-evict, latency for token fetch dropped ~200ms.

Alex G.: I'm seeing residual noise from alert rule "prefix_kv_eviction_spike" — it triggered twice during mitigation and paged two people. We should adjust paging so on-call isn't paged for transient spikes during rollouts.

Priya N.: agree. Proposing tuning: change alert to fire only if eviction_spike > 1000 AND sustained for 5m, or if combined with hit_rate < 20% for 3m. Also add a separate non-paging warning for 1-3m transients.

Maria S.: that sounds right. We need to avoid alert fatigue. Also create a dedicated Grafana panel for prefix hot-keys and an alert that triggers when a single prefix accounts for >40% of evictions.

Chris L.: drafting rule; example PromQL snippets for the new panels/alerts:
```promql
# live prefix hit rate (per prefix)
sum by(prefix) (rate(redwood_cache_hits_total{cache="prefix-kv-store"}[5m]))
/
sum by(prefix) (rate(redwood_cache_requests_total{cache="prefix-kv-store"}[5m]))

# eviction spike threshold per region
sum by(region) (increase(redwood_cache_evictions_total{cache="prefix-kv-store"}[5m]))
```

Priya N.: thanks. For the paging change: change alert annotations to "severity: warning" for single-sample spikes and only escalate to paging if the sustained condition is met. I'll open a quick PR to ops-alerts.

Alex G.: note for postmortem — root cause likely a regression in the per-prefix TTL churn from the model shard rollout that created many new prefixes (small cardinality explosion). we should add a pre-deploy check for prefix cardinality delta.

Maria S.: agreed. Customer impact summary for oncall notes: ~42 requests impacted across 2 customers, increased 5xx rate for streaming endpoints between 11:12–11:36, mitigated by config soft-evict and capacity bump. no data exfiltration, no long-term degradation.

Priya N.: follow-ups I will own: 1) PR to adjust alert thresholds and paging behavior (ops-alerts). 2) New Grafana dashboard panel for prefix hot-key heatmap and per-prefix hit-rate. 3) Post-incident ticket to add pre-deploy prefix-cardinality check. Assigning Maria for customer comms draft.

Maria S.: taking customer comms. I'll draft an email/console message for org-53 and org-77 with timeline + remediation steps.

Chris L.: created a short-lived escalation doc in /confluence/incidents/1918579200 for the runbook changes. Also added a note to avoid increasing max_entries globally without a cap (that can cause memory pressure).

eng-sre-bot: incident-bot closed paging after mitigation window.

Priya N.: wrapping up — I'll merge the alert PR with a 10m delayed rollout so we don't mute other regions inadvertently. We should schedule a follow-up postmortem tomorrow. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Alex G.: thanks. I'll keep the new panels in a temp dashboard and transfer to shared ops dash once validated.

Maria S.: handing off to night oncall @Chris L. for monitoring. Chris, make sure the new non-paging warning behaves as expected overnight; escalate to me if anything spikes back.

Chris L.: taking handoff. noted.
